sections.h2: Which offices do Green County owners deal with?
sections.html:
Two courthouse-area offices split the job in Green County. The Green County Sheriff collects the bill at 203 W Court Street, Greensburg, KY 42743, phone (270) 932-5641. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assesses every parcel from 103 South 1st Street in Greensburg, phone (270) 932-7518.

The PVA values property and keeps the records. The sheriff takes payment. Call the PVA for address changes, exemption forms and questions about how a value was reached, and call ahead to either office to confirm its hours.

The Census counts 4,421 households in Green County, so a phone call to either office is the quickest way to confirm a payoff or a parcel record before you list.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Green County itself?
sections.html:
South central Kentucky holds Green County, whose only incorporated city is the seat, Greensburg. Summersville is a census-designated place, and every resident counted in 2020 lived in a rural area. The county was formed on December 20, 1792, from parts of Lincoln and Nelson counties, and it later gave up land to create Adair, Cumberland and Taylor counties.

The county government places it twenty miles north of Lindsey Wilson College in Adair County and twelve miles west of Campbellsville University in Taylor County. The land covers about 286 square miles, and the Green River runs across it from east to west. The county government describes terrain that ranges from flat and gently rolling to steep and rocky, and it points to Green River Lake, American Legion Park on the river and Wyatt Jeffries Woods as local draws. Greensburg's 1804 brick courthouse, the oldest in the state according to Wikipedia, stands in the Downtown Greensburg Historic District, and the current courthouse dates from 1931. Cow Days brings crowds to town the third weekend of September.

History runs deep here. The Cumberland Trace, an early road from Lincoln County toward Nashville, crosses the county, and an oil boom from 1958 into the early 1960s lifted the local economy enough that temporary air strips were built at Summersville and Pierce. The 445-foot Goose Creek Footbridge, built in the late 1920s, links the town square to the old train depot. Green County was also dry until 2015.

Census QuickFacts gives the housing numbers sellers will meet:

  • July 2025 estimate: 11,644 residents, a 4.8 percent gain on the 2020 base.
  • Homes lived in by their owners: 77.6 percent, at 2.54 people per household.
  • Median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024: $125,000.
  • Median owner costs: $955 a month with a mortgage and $361 without one.
  • Median gross rent: $610. Median household income: $46,798. Persons in poverty: 17.9 percent.

The county sits on the Central and Eastern time zone line, with LaRue and Taylor counties to the north on Eastern time, so check which clock an appointment uses.

sections.h2: How does the Green County tax year run?
sections.html:
The PVA's online calendar begins with the January 1 assessment date and finishes with the sheriff's settlement the next September. For a homeowner the milestones are mid-September, when the sheriff receives bills, November 1, when the discount ends, and January 1, when penalties begin. The clerk's sale of delinquent certificates is listed for July 14 through August 28.

Green County real estate tax calendar (source: Green County PVA website)
StepDate or window
Public inspection of the roll, with PVA conferences13 days from the first Monday in May, Saturdays included
Assessment appeals board sits5 days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection
Bills handed to the sheriffBy September 15
Discounted paymentBy November 1
Payment at face amountNovember 2 to December 31
Five percent penaltyJanuary 1 to 31
Ten percent penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff's add-onAfter January 31
Sheriff stops collecting; bills go to the clerkApril 15, at close of business
Sheriff's settlementBy September 1

When bills mail late, the state may switch to a slower schedule with a 30-day stage for each step.

sections.h2: What is the appeal route for a Green County value?
sections.html:
See the Green County PVA, then the county clerk. Kentucky shuts the local board's door on anyone who skipped the conference, and conferences happen during that May inspection window.

  • Have the PVA explain the number, then state your own. The conference record shows the starting value, your claim and any changes both sides accept.
  • File with the clerk before the close of the workday that follows the inspection period.
  • Show up at the hearing with proof: lot and building details, insurance papers, build costs and listings of comparable houses.
  • If the board raises or cuts the value, it owes you a written reason.

A professional paid to speak for you must fit the state's list of qualified representatives and hold your written authorization. Skipping the filing or the hearing ends the path to the Kentucky Claims Commission. A late-finishing case can bring a supplemental bill if the board lands above your claim.

sections.h2: Which Green County property is exempt?
sections.html:
Section 170 of Kentucky's constitution, which the Green County PVA site reproduces, exempts public property in public use, burial grounds, church property, charities, schools not run for gain, public libraries, household goods and crops in the producer's hands. A separate break covers owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who keep the house as a permanent residence.

It is worth $49,100 in assessment years 2025 and 2026. At Green County's Census median of $125,000, a qualifying owner is taxed on $75,900. Apply through the PVA with a birth certificate, license or passport. Disability claims need payments received through the whole assessment period and a yearly renewal, except for service-connected veterans and owners with a permanent total disability finding.

The break matters locally. Green County's median age was 44.6 in 2020, and 21.1 percent of residents had reached 65, so many owners may qualify.

If you move out, give the PVA your new mailing address so assessment notices and tax bills reach you.

sections.h2: What if a Green County house sells with tax still owed?
sections.html:
The debt rides with the land, so it passes to the buyer unless it is cleared first. The owner on January 1 is personally liable, and a delinquent bill's lien can survive 11 years, as KRS 134.015 and 134.420 provide, whoever holds title.

Timing drives the cost. Pay the sheriff before April 15 and you owe only the penalties already earned. After the transfer, the clerk adds 1 percent monthly interest, a 10 percent commission, a county attorney commission and a lien fee. The state's sample shows how fast it grows: $1,000 turns into $1,387.79 almost at once and $1,611.30 once the attorney's first notice goes out.

The county attorney writes at the 30-day and 60-day marks, and a sale follows 90 to 135 days after the transfer. Get both payoffs in writing before listing, and let the closing agent pay them from the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: When does the Green County discount end?
faqs.a: On November 1. The calendar lets owners pay 2 percent less through then, face amount from the next day to December 31, and adds 5 percent in January.

faqs.q: Who takes tax payments in Green County?
faqs.a: The Green County Sheriff, at 203 W Court Street in Greensburg, phone (270) 932-5641. The PVA at (270) 932-7518 values property and handles exemptions but takes no payments.

faqs.q: What happens to a Green County bill after January 31?
faqs.a: After January 31 the PVA calendar adds a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent sheriff fee. The clerk takes over on April 15 and charges monthly interest.

faqs.q: How large is the Green County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, get $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. At the $125,000 median, that leaves $75,900 taxable.

faqs.q: When does Green County sell delinquent tax bills?
faqs.a: The standard calendar lists July 14 through August 28, which falls 90 to 135 days after the April 15 handoff to the clerk.
